Synopsis:
    European equities rebounded modestly (+0.5%, STOXX 600 at 649.1) after three losing sessions, aided by a partial easing in bond yields. The backdrop remains strained: an Iran war escalation has kept oil above $95/bbl, fueling persistent inflation concerns and raising the bar for central bank pivots. The ECB is widely expected to hike to 2.5% next week with two further hikes priced in by mid-2027. In the US, hawkish signals from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh have lifted rate hike bets, with Friday's NFP report the next key catalyst. Stock-level movers include Soitec (+10.3% on upgraded revenue outlook), WPP and Publicis (PepsiCo account win), while luxury names lagged. Commerzbank announced a €1.2B buyback; Deutsche Telekom gained on Elliott stake-building.
